title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck is studying the 'structure at infinity' of the moduli stacks M_{g,ν}. The compactifying boundary is a normal-crossings divisor, stratified by the loci D_d (codimension d, where d branches meet) and their open parts D*_d = D_d minus D_{d+1}. For a pair of strata A ⊂ R he has topoi V_{A,R}, the tubular neighbourhood of A in R, and V*_{A,R}, the deleted (punctured) tubular neighbourhood. These are meant to encode the homotopy types (étale or profinite) of neighbourhoods at infinity.

Definition (273). The previous page introduced an intermediate stratum A ⊂ B ⊂ R. On this page Grothendieck defines a 'mixed' topos V^{B(*)}_{A,R} as the fibre product of two maps over V_{B,R}:
- V_{A,R} → V_{B,R}, the canonical map from the neighbourhood of A to the neighbourhood of B;
- V*_{B,R} → V_{B,R}, the inclusion of the deleted neighbourhood of B.
Geometrically it is the tubular neighbourhood of A in R with B removed: punctured in the directions transverse to B, unpunctured in the directions of B transverse to A.

Local model (next page). Take X = C×C, A = the origin, B = Δ1 = {y=0}. Then
- U_{A,X} = D×D;
- U*_{Δ1,X} = C×D*;
- U^{Δ1}_{A,X} = D×D*, which is exactly their intersection.
This confirms the fibre-product reading.

General indexing (274)–(276). In the combinatorial situation the strata are indexed by decreasing sequences of codimensions. A three-step flag d''_* ⊂ d'_* ⊂ d_* (each of the form d_0 > ... > d_r) gives the closed strata D_{d_*} → D_{d'_*} → D_{d''_*}. Grothendieck defines V^{d'_*}_{d_*,d''_*} as the analogous fibre product, (276):
- tubular neighbourhood of D*_{d_*} in D_{d''_*};
- intersected with the deleted neighbourhood of D_{d'_*} in D_{d''_*}.
He notes in the margin that the base must be the open stratum D*_{d_*}, not D_{d_*}: 'attention aux *'.

NB. He asks whether the topos depends only on d_*, d'_0 and d''_0, with d_0 ≥ d'_0 ≥ d''_0 ≥ 0, and in the margin decides to write V^{d'_0}_{d_*,d''_0}. This is right for normal crossings. Locally the topos is (open stratum) × D^{d_0-d'_0} × (D*)^{d'_0-d''_0}. Homotopically it is a (D*)^{d'_0-d''_0}, i.e. torus, fibration over the stratum. It sees only how many transverse coordinates are punctured and how many are not.

Purpose. To list all 'types' of neighbourhood topoi at infinity, together with the restriction and specialisation maps between them. This gives a combinatorial gluing description of the homotopy type of M_{g,ν} near the boundary. The next page enumerates the 16 types for the model C^2.
errors: The NB is posed as a question; it is correct locally for normal-crossings strata, but only up to the stratum factor. Globally the torus fibration may be twisted (e.g. by monodromy permuting divisor branches on the stack), so dependence 'only on d_*, d'_0, d''_0' should be read as dependence on the local type, not as an identification of topoi.

In (276) the indices on the corners are inconsistent in the draft (primes and stars misplaced: D'_d, D''_d versus D_{d'_*}, D_{d''_*}). Grothendieck himself flags the star problem in the bracketed remark. This is a notational slip, not a mathematical error.

ideas.what: Tubular and deleted-tubular neighbourhood topoi of strata of a normal-crossings boundary of M_{g,ν}, used to describe the 'structure at infinity'
ideas.modern_name: homotopy links / punctured tubular neighbourhoods; Kato–Nakayama (real oriented blow-up) Betti realisation of log structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (homotopy links, 1988); Kato–Nakayama (1999); in the moduli setting Harvey, Ivanov, Looijenga, Ebert–Giansiracusa
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to tubular neighbourhoods at infinity of M_{g,ν} and to the Teichmüller tower, without this formalism

ideas.what: Mixed neighbourhood V^{B(*)}_{A,R}: tubular neighbourhood of A in R, punctured along an intermediate stratum B, defined as a fibre product of topoi
ideas.modern_name: partial real blow-up / generalised (multi-stratum) homotopy links in stratified homotopy theory, cf. the exit-path ∞-category
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn; Woolf; Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A); Treumann; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka

ideas.what: Observation that the mixed topos depends only on the triple of codimensions (d_0 ≥ d'_0 ≥ d''_0), i.e. a local type D^a × (D*)^b over the stratum
ideas.modern_name: local product structure of log / normal-crossings neighbourhoods (torus fibrations of rank = number of punctured directions)

missed.claim: Grothendieck organises neighbourhood topoi of a normal-crossings boundary into a family indexed by three-step flags of strata, with partially punctured neighbourhoods as fibre products of topoi. This is essentially the data of generalised homotopy links and exit-path gluing, or equivalently of the Kato–Nakayama space restricted to strata, set up topos-theoretically for the purpose of profinite and Galois-theoretic study of M_{g,ν} at infinity. The explicit flag-indexed fibre-product formalism for the moduli boundary, aimed at tangential-basepoint-type Galois actions, is not in the record as Grothendieck's.
missed.quote: Je vais désigner par V_{A,R}^{B(*)} le topos correspondant, qui peut se décrire comme un produit fibré
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates the stratified / exit-path description of the boundary of M_{g,ν}, as used for profinite Teichmüller theory and Grothendieck–Teichmüller actions on boundary groupoids. It is mainly of historical interest, since the mathematics is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful set-up of mixed punctured/unpunctured tubular-neighbourhood topoi for normal-crossings strata. It is conceptually in line with later stratified homotopy theory (homotopy links, exit paths, Kato–Nakayama), but the content is local and essentially routine for a specialist; its interest is historical anticipation.
transcription_corrections: (275) should read D_{d_*} → D_{d'_*} → D_{d''_*} (no prime on the letter D).

The fragment around (274) likely reads 'Ce topos, dans la situation générale précédente, correspondant à une subdivision {d''_* ⊂ d'_* ⊂ d_*}', with d''_* = {d''_0 > ... > d''_{r''}}, d'_* = {d'_0 > ... > d'_{r'}} and d_* = {d_0 > ... > d_r} written under the respective terms.
Bracketed remark: roughly 'attention aux * en cavalier – on ne voit pas [de place pour] D_{d_*}! attention – l'écriture doit être D*_{d_*}!'
The final NB reads: 'NB ce topos ne dépend en fait que des d_*, d'_0, d''_0, où d_0 ≥ d'_0 ≥ d''_0 ≥ 0 ?'
The left margin reads: 'On va donc noter ce topos V^{d'_0}_{d_*,d''_0}'.
The top-right note in (276) seems to read 'ici par d_* car ...', explaining the index choice on the right-hand column.
